channel.title: The Minnesota Star Tribune - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Minnesota Star Tribune (startribune.com)

item.title: Anderson: Wolves, eagles, rodents — gut piles left behind by successful deer hunters draw big crowds
item.description: A U of M study involves camera-toting hunters who document what happens to awful “offal” — or gut piles.

item.title: Minnesotan’s Ice Mile swim illuminates a new level of extreme
item.description: The sport is no stunt, as swimmer Mackenzie Koeck and her support crew learned in the yearlong runup of preparation.

item.title: ‘Forever chemicals’ slam small cities with big water bills as they surface farther from 3M sites
item.description: Apple Valley will likely hike water rates to fund a $100 million project to rid its wells of PFAS.

item.title: Holiday Cookie Finder: Now updated with the 2025 winning recipes
item.description: Plus, more than 100 other recipes to use this holiday season — and all year long

item.title: Burcum: A city of 24,000 but nowhere to deliver a baby
item.description: As Faribault joins the list of cities without a birth center, it may be time for the Legislature to get involved.

item.title: A 1,200-mile journey into David Lynch’s creative and spiritual Midwest
item.description: The visionary filmmaker’s art looked at the broken psyche inside America. His life showed a way to fix it.

item.title: Flight carrying federal detainees leaves Minnesota as ICE activity escalates
item.description: The Twin Cities saw immigration enforcement operations targeting Somalis and Latinos carried out this week by federal agents.

item.title: St. Paul alleges contractor made off with nearly $1M meant for financial literacy lessons
item.description: A federal lawsuit alleges a Maryland company never delivered the lessons meant to tie into the city’s college savings program for newborns.

item.title: Minnesota’s hemp rules could offer a model for federal regulation as ban looms
item.description: Lawmakers and business owners say Minnesota’s testing, age limits and potency caps show what a safe national framework could look like — if the federal ban doesn’t erase it first.

item.title: Republican state senator admonishes Trump for calling Somalis ‘garbage,’ invites him to Minnesota
item.description: Sen. Jim Abeler of Anoka tells the president: ‘No man, woman or child is more or less in the eyes of our Lord.’
